sentences: GFX10 `image_sample_d` with `a16` keeps the non-G16 gradients as f32 and packs the following coordinates as f16 pairs, following LLVM's GFX10 operand layout.
`test_a16_sample_gradients_use_full_vgprs` checks the emitted gradient operands, and `ps_texture_grad_a16` checks coordinate selection with a single-mip texture on RTX 5080.

The same holds for every extra argument before the coordinates (LLVM `getAddrSizeMIMGOp`: one word each, then the gradients, then the packed halves; llvm-mc takes `v[0:2]` for a 2D `image_sample_c_b ... a16`): an `image_sample_b` bias keeps its VGPR with the f16 in the low half, an `image_sample_c_lz` z-compare its f32 VGPR, and `image_sample_d_cl` its four f32 gradients, with the clamp the half right after the coordinates (an f16 pad may follow it).
Until 2026-11-21 those were unpacked as pairs too, and the clamp was taken from the last half.

GPU-checked on an NVIDIA GeForce RTX 2060 SUPER (Linux, driver 620.70.06) with `ps_texture_bias_a16`, `ps_sample_c_lz_a16` (`vk_texture_test dref_a16`) and `ps_texture_grad_cl_a16`, which draws on the `--two-mip` texture with the clamp 0 on the left half and 1 on the right: 4096/4096 pixels exact each.

The old reading got 4,032 bias pixels and both depth-compare results in 2,048 pixels wrong, a clamp taken from the pad read mip 1 on the left half, and the sample without its clamp mip 0 on the right half (2,048 pixels each).
